metadata.title: Canvas Making Process
metadata.description: Learn about our premium canvas production process - from material selection to quality control, see how we craft our high-quality canvas prints.

hero.title: How We Make Our Canvases
hero.description: Discover the craftsmanship and attention to detail that goes into every canvas we produce.

materials.title: Selecting Premium Materials
materials.description: We start with carefully selected, high-grade cotton blend canvas. Each roll is inspected for quality and consistency, ensuring that only the finest materials make it to our production floor. Our canvas has an opacity of up to 75%, over 7x higher than Best Canvas.

printing.title: High Quality Printing Process
printing.description: We utilise advanced Canon printing technology to deliver exceptional colour vibrancy and durability. After printing your image using UVgel ink, the print undergoes UV LED curing. The result? A durable, flexible finish that needs no further protection. It's so durable, our canvases are backed by our 30-year print quality guarantee!

frame.title: Custom Stretcher Frame Assembly
frame.description: Our skilled craftsmen construct sturdy stretcher frames from premium wood, precisely cut and joined to create the foundation of your canvas. Each corner is reinforced for lasting durability.

stretching.title: Professional Stretching Process
stretching.description: Using specialised equipment and techniques, we stretch the canvas over the frame with perfect tension. This critical step ensures your canvas will maintain its shape and stability over time.

quality.title: Quality Control
quality.description: Every canvas undergoes rigorous quality checks throughout the production process. We examine tension, corner folds, and overall construction to ensure each piece meets our exacting standards.

cta.title: Ready to Experience Our Quality?
cta.description: Each canvas is crafted with care and backed by our satisfaction guarantee.

imageQuality.question: How do I know if my image quality is good enough?
imageQuality.answer: Our system automatically checks your image resolution and shows a quality indicator (Poor, Normal or Perfect) when you select a canvas size. We recommend 'Perfect' quality for the best results.

depthDifference.question: What's the difference between Regular and Gallery depth?
depthDifference.answer: Regular depth (0.75 inches) is our standard option, while Gallery depth (1.5 inches) creates a more dramatic, museum-like appearance with deeper sides.

localPickupAvailable.question: Do you offer local pickup?
localPickupAvailable.answer: Yes! We offer free local pickup at our Quebec City location during business hours (Monday-Friday, 9am-5pm EST). You'll receive an email when your order is ready.

satisfaction.question: What if I'm not satisfied with my canvas?

durability.question: How long will my canvas last?

deliveryTime.question: How long does delivery take?

qualitySection.title: Why our canvas feels different
qualitySection.description: Most online canvas prints look similar on screen, but feel very different in real life. We focus on the materials and print process so your canvas actually looks and feels premium when it's on the wall.

premiumCanvas.title: Premium cotton-blend canvas
premiumCanvas.description: We use a high-density cotton-blend canvas with up to 75% opacity. That means richer colour, cleaner whites and far less show-through than lightweight budget canvases.

archivalPrinting.title: Archival-grade printing
archivalPrinting.description: Your photo is printed with Canon UVgel technology for sharp detail, deep blacks and no odour. We guarantee it will not fade for 30+ years in typical home conditions.

handStretched.title: Hand-stretched in Quebec City
handStretched.description: Every canvas is printed, stretched and finished in our Quebec City studio on custom wooden stretcher bars, with tight tension and crisp, clean corners.

readyToHang.title: Ready to hang, built to last
readyToHang.description: Each canvas arrives ready to hang with hardware included, and is checked by our team before it leaves the workshop.

comparisonSection.title: Canvas Print Shop vs cheap canvas prints
comparisonSection.description: Not all canvases are made the same. Here's how our canvases compare to the typical discount canvas prints you see online.

material.ours: Premium cotton-blend canvas with high opacity.
material.theirs: Lightweight polyester canvas with more show-through.

opacity.ours: Up to 75% opacity for rich colour and clean whites.
opacity.theirs: Lower opacity, more visible texture and show-through on light walls.

technology.ours: Canon UVgel printing for sharp detail and long-lasting colour.
technology.theirs: Standard dye or solvent printing, more prone to fading.

frames.ours: Custom stretcher bars, hand-stretched and inspected in our Quebec City studio.
frames.theirs: Generic frames, often machine-stretched with less quality control.

origin.theirs: Often produced in high-volume overseas facilities.

guarantee.ours: 30-year print quality guarantee and 30-day satisfaction guarantee.
guarantee.theirs: Shorter warranties and more limited support.

comparisonSection.footer: Designed, printed and finished in Canada, backed by a 30-year print quality guarantee.

intro.title: Delivering canvas prints to Montreal
intro.body: Montreal orders are printed and hand-stretched at our Lac-Saint-Charles studio and shipped by courier, whether you are in the Plateau, Rosemont, Verdun or the West Island. Because we print in Quebec rather than importing from an overseas plant, your canvas never clears customs and never sits in a consolidation warehouse.

one.description: Order today and your canvas typically reaches Montreal within 5 to 10 business days — production and shipping combined — packed flat and ready to hang.

two.title: Printed in Quebec, not overseas
two.description: No customs, no cross-border duty and no consolidation warehouse. Your file is printed and stretched by the same team.

three.title: 30-year fade guarantee
three.description: Canon Colorado UVgel ink on cotton-blend canvas, rated to hold its colour for 30 years indoors.

items.title: Total time
items.description: 5 to 10 business days from order to delivery — roughly one to two weeks — covering production and shipping together.

items.title: Made to order
items.description: Nothing is pre-printed or warehoused. Your file goes through prepress, then the canvas is printed, hand-stretched and packed for you.

items.title: Packaging
items.description: Shipped flat in a rigid corner-protected carton, never rolled in a tube.

faq.q: How long does delivery to Montreal take?
faq.a: Typically 5 to 10 business days from the moment you order — about one to two weeks — covering production and shipping. If you need it for a specific date, give yourself a little more room than that.

faq.q: Do you charge extra to ship to Montreal?
faq.a: No. Shipping is priced the same across our entire Quebec and Ontario delivery area, and free shipping promotions apply here too.

faq.q: Do you deliver outside Quebec and Ontario?
faq.a: Not at present. We deliver throughout Quebec and Ontario so we can keep transit times short and avoid damage in long-haul freight.

faq.q: Does the canvas arrive ready to hang?
faq.a: Yes. It is stretched on a solid wood frame with hanging hardware already fitted, packed flat rather than rolled.

intro.title: Choosing which wedding photo to print
intro.body:
Wedding galleries are overwhelming precisely because they are complete. The images that work best on canvas are rarely the formal group shots — they are the ones with a single clear subject and some breathing room around it: the first look, a candid during the speeches, the two of you leaving.

Canvas is a matte surface, which is an advantage here. Wedding photography tends to be high-contrast with bright whites in the dress, and a glossy print will throw glare across exactly that area under ceiling lights. A matte canvas holds the detail in the fabric instead.

If your photographer supplied both edited JPEGs and RAW files, send the edited JPEG. It reflects the colour grading you paid for, and our printer profiles handle it without further adjustment.

intro.title: Making a family photo work on canvas
intro.body:
Family photos are usually taken for the people in them rather than for the wall, which means the composition needs a second look before printing. Check where everyone's heads sit in the frame: if they are near the top edge, a gallery wrap will pull part of that around the side of the stretcher.

Group shots generally do better at 24x36 or larger. At 16x20 an eight-person photo renders each face at roughly the size of a coin, and the image reads as a crowd rather than as your family.

Mixed indoor lighting is the other common issue — a photo shot half under a window and half under warm bulbs will show that split more plainly on canvas than on a screen. We correct obvious colour casts as part of standard prepress, at no extra cost.

intro.title: Why canvas suits pet photography
intro.body:
Fur is texture, and canvas is a textured surface — the two work together in a way that glossy photo paper does not. A matte canvas softens the harsh edge that flash photography often leaves on a dark coat, and it holds detail in black fur, which is the hardest thing to print well.

The practical challenge with pet photos is usually motion blur rather than resolution. Look at the eyes at full zoom before uploading: if they are sharp, the print will be fine even if the tail is not. If the whole frame is soft, no amount of enlargement will fix it.

Close crops work better than full-body shots. A head-and-shoulders composition at 16x20 has far more presence than a full-length photo of a small dog in a large room.

intro.title: Sizing artwork above a bed
intro.body:
Above-bed placement has a clear rule of thumb: the artwork should span roughly two-thirds the width of the bed, with the bottom edge sitting about 15 to 25 cm above the headboard. For a queen bed that points to a 24x36 canvas. For a king, either a 36x48 or two 24x36 canvases hung as a pair.

Bedrooms are also the room where surface finish matters most. Bedside lamps sit low and throw light upward at exactly the angle that produces glare on a glossy print. Canvas is matte by nature, so it stays readable from the bed rather than turning into a reflective panel.

On subject matter, bedrooms tend to suit calmer images — landscapes, abstracts, a single portrait — better than busy, high-contrast compositions.

intro.body:
The most common mistake in living rooms is hanging something too small. A standard three-seat sofa is around 210 cm wide, which calls for artwork spanning roughly 140 cm — that is a 36x48 canvas, or two 24x36 canvases hung together with a small gap.

Height matters too. The bottom edge of the canvas should sit 15 to 25 cm above the back of the sofa. Higher than that and the piece floats free of the furniture; lower and people knock it with their heads.

Living rooms usually have the most natural light in the house, which is where our UVgel ink earns its keep. It carries a 30-year fade guarantee, so a canvas on a south-facing wall will not go magenta after a couple of summers the way dye-based prints do.

intro.title: What changes when a canvas gets large
intro.body:
Two things fail on cheap large canvases: the frame and the file. We address both. Above 24x36 we build on a reinforced stretcher with a centre brace, because unbraced bars on a wide canvas bow inward over a year or two and the canvas goes slack.

Resolution is the other constraint. A 36x48 needs roughly 3600 × 4800 pixels to hold detail at normal viewing distance. That said, large prints are viewed from further away, so the requirement is more forgiving than the arithmetic suggests — we assess every file individually and tell you before we print rather than after.

Large canvases ship flat in a rigid carton with reinforced corners, not rolled in a tube. A rolled canvas has to be re-stretched at the other end, which is a job for a framing shop.

intro.title: Floater frames versus gallery wrap
intro.body:
A gallery wrap pulls the image around the sides of the stretcher bars and hangs with no frame at all — clean, modern, and the more common choice. A floater frame instead surrounds the stretched canvas with a thin border, leaving a small visible gap so the canvas appears to sit inside the frame rather than being clamped by it.

The practical reason to choose framed over gallery wrap is composition. Gallery wrap consumes roughly 1.5 inches of image on every edge. If your photo has a subject close to the border, or text, or a horizon you do not want bending around a corner, the frame keeps the full image flat and visible.

Framed canvases ship ready to hang with hardware attached, exactly like the unframed ones. There is no assembly.

Mass-produced wall art is designed to be inoffensive in any room, which is exactly why it rarely holds anyone's attention. Photographs you took have the opposite quality: they mean something specific, and they are the only copy in existence.

If you are assembling a gallery wall, the usual approach is one larger anchor piece with two or three smaller canvases arranged around it, keeping 5 to 8 cm of spacing throughout. A 24x36 anchor with a pair of 16x20 canvases is a reliable starting configuration.

Consistency matters more than matching. Canvases printed in the same run share the same colour handling, so a set ordered together will hang as a group rather than looking like three separate purchases.

intro.title: What gallery wrap actually means
intro.body:
Gallery wrap means the printed image continues around the sides of the stretcher bars and is stapled on the back, so no staples or raw canvas are visible from any angle. The result hangs without a frame and sits slightly proud of the wall.

The trade-off is that roughly 1.5 inches of image on each edge ends up on the side of the frame rather than facing forward. We account for this in prepress by checking your composition before printing — if a face, a horizon or text falls inside that margin, we will tell you and suggest the framed option instead.

Stretching is done by hand over kiln-dried solid wood. Machine-stretched canvas from high-volume printers tends to tension unevenly, which shows up months later as a visible ripple across the face.
